result: In 40 ME patients vs 40 controls, LV end-diastolic and end-systolic diameters, stroke volume index, cardiac index and LV mass index were all smaller; small LVEDD (<40 mm) in 45% vs 3% and cardiac index <2 in 53% vs 8%; ejection fraction normal; OI in 35/36.
reason: Independent echo cohort, same measure (smaller LV and stroke volume, normal EF); Miwa 2015 is not the cited Miwa 2026

result: In 120 adolescents with CFS vs 39 healthy controls (NorCAPITAL), pressure pain thresholds by algometry were significantly lower and severe pain more prevalent.
reason: Lower pressure pain thresholds replicate the generalised hyperalgesia part of the claim in an independent adolescent cohort; no CPM or post-exercise data

result: In 30 adolescents with CFS vs 39 controls, supine resting heart rate and blood pressure were higher and HRV indices lower; imagined standing raised LF and LF/HF more in CFS.
reason: Same measures (resting HR higher, HRV lower), same direction, independent small cohort

result: Supine stroke index was lower in 30 adolescents with CFS than 39 controls, but the response to 20-degree head-up tilt was identical between groups.
reason: Replicates lower resting stroke volume; the mild 20-degree tilt showed no excess fall, so it does not support the tilt part of the claim

result: Total daily salivary cortisol output (AUC) was lower in 46 adolescents with CFS than 33 matched controls, with no difference in awakening response; output rose to normal 6 months after CBT guided self-help (n=21).
reason: Same measure (salivary cortisol) lower in an independent adolescent cohort; awakening response itself was not different

result: In a blinded multi-site prospective study, murine retroviral sequences were found in 5/72 CFS (6.7%) vs 2/37 controls (5.4%), p=1, and appeared to be endogenous mouse DNA contamination in PCR reagents, not XMRV or pMLV.
reason: Independent blinded study, same test, supports the no-association/contamination conclusion; not among cited studies

result: Systematic review of 27 case-control studies concluded autonomic responses, notably the heart rate response to head-up tilt, differ between CFS and controls.
reason: Abstract reports no resting HR or HF-HRV data; too thin to test this finding

result: Systematic review of 27 case-control studies (quality 50-71%) concluded the tilt heart rate response differs in CFS, supporting increased POTS prevalence, without giving rates.
reason: No prevalence figures; abstract too thin to test the claim about POTS rates

result: In 22 ME/CFS patients, a second CPET 24 h later showed falls in VO2peak (13.8%), HRpeak (9 bpm), work at peak (12.5%), VO2 at VT (15.8%) and work at VT (21.3%), with peak RER >=1.1 on both tests.
reason: Same 2-day CPET measures, same direction; small and without a control group; Keller 2014 is distinct from cited Keller 2024

result: In 22 ME/CFS patients, CPET measures fell on a repeat test 24 h later (VO2peak -13.8%, work at VT -21.3%).
reason: Does not measure PEM onset, duration or recovery time; already covered by the two-day CPET link
